analysis.title: "Higher Probability Of VIX 25 Than SPX -2%": Hedge Funds Dump Tech As Goldman Finds Records Everywhere Except Conviction
key_insights: S&P 500 rose 1.2% on the week to 7,811, Nasdaq 100 rose 0.2% and Russell 2000 fell 0.9%. Goldman desks flagged record or near-record readings in Mag7 hedge fund exposure, Russell 2000 futures shorts, IWM short interest, EWZ volume and fixed income ETF volume share.

Goldman prime book: US equities were slightly net sold (-0.1 SDs) and single stocks were net sold for a third straight week, with short sales outpacing long buys 2 to 1. Info Tech was by far the most net sold sector (-1.0 SDs), driven by both long and short sales, especially on Thursday Oct 8 after the FT report that OpenAI revenues were disappointing.

Hedge funds net bought US Industrials at the fastest pace since early January (+1.8 SDs) after 5 straight weeks of selling, almost entirely via long buys led by Aerospace & Defense, Construction & Engineering, Airlines and Industrial Conglomerates.
Within tech, Tech Hardware and Semis were most sold and Software was most bought. Goldman's Software vs Semis pair rose 11.8% on the week, and Software outperformed Semis by about 800 bps.

US fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 3.8 points to 213%. Net leverage rose 0.5 points to 46.9%, still in the 2nd percentile of the past year. The long/short ratio slipped 0.3% to 1.565, in the 1st percentile on a five-year lookback.

Average fundamental L/S fund lost 0.70% between Oct 2 and Oct 8 while MSCI World gained 0.78%. Fundamental L/S is up 11.82% YTD, trailing MSCI (12.42%) and the S&P (14.45%). Systematic funds rose 0.82% on the week and are up 21.40% YTD.

Hedge fund Mag7 positioning moved from a YTD low of 14% in June to a record 22% of US exposure on Goldman's Prime book. Morgan Stanley prime data shows Info Tech at 32% of hedge funds' North America net exposure, the 98th percentile since 2010.

Morgan Stanley prime data has Health Care at the 3rd percentile of the past year and Financials at the 100th. Goldman says hedge funds de-grossed Health Care for a 4th straight week, and Biotech de-grossing is the largest in more than five years on a trailing 8-week basis. The Biotech long/short ratio fell to 3.22 from a December peak of 5.36.

Q3 earnings season starts Tuesday with the big banks. Consensus expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y, the highest since 2021, versus 9% y/y for the median stock (14% in Q2). Micron and Nvidia account for about a third of the quarter's earnings growth.

Last quarter beats were rewarded with one of the smallest outperformances vs the S&P on record (35bps vs 95bps historically). Micron reported 1,003% EPS growth, beat across the board and had a muted reaction.

Financials have underperformed into their prints (XLF -6.5% from highs while SPX hit records). The ratio of recent drawdown to the earnings-day straddle is about 5x, which Goldman's derivatives desk calls implied move cheap. Morgan Stanley is down 20% from its high and priced for a 3.7% move, and Bank of America is down 19% and priced for 3.4%.

Goldman's Christian DeGrasse says bank sentiment has notably turned cautious, and the debate is whether the expected 3Q activity slowdown is a brief air pocket or a prolonged slowdown. Credit risk is viewed as benign with one eye open on CRE.
Morgan Stanley's Nick Savone says US banks are the most oversold relative to the S&P since 1993, with a 14-day RSI around 27, and BKX forward P/E is below its 10-year median.

Goldman's derivatives desk: VIX upside convexity is extremely bid while SPX downside convexity remains very offered. An index vol colleague said there is almost a higher probability of VIX 25+ than SPX -2%. Low realized correlation and high dispersion explain the gap.
Most index implied vols ended the week at 2-3 month lows. Thursday was one of the first sessions QQQ vol fell as QQQ spot rose. Nomura's Charlie McElligott said the only fear is of the right-tail.

Russell 2000 futures positioning is at record shorts and IWM short interest is at record highs, while IWM vol is below the 10th percentile. Goldman's derivatives desk likes owning IWM calls for those running short small cap delta.

Nasdaq's funding premium to the S&P reached a 98% 1-year rank on the Oct 8 close, suggesting leveraged long positioning increased. Asset managers sold $3.2BN of index futures between Sep 8 and Sep 29 alongside higher index prices, taking the correlation between their gross longs and price to effectively nil.

Goldman futures desk: long bonds may have found a bottom after selling off since Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech on 8/28. OpenAI revenue restatement headlines prompted the Thursday rally in bond futures, supporting the view that expected AI-related bond issuance has pushed up long-term UST yields.
Asset manager shorts in the long bond rose sharply since mid-September. Short covering could support bonds into early next week, but the rally must survive Tuesday's CPI.

Gold rose 1.3% on the week and has held above $4,100/oz despite US real rates at multi-decade highs. Systematic strategies are at the 0th percentile on a 1-year lookback and CFTC managed money net length is back to average. Goldman's futures desk says adding length in gold looks increasingly attractive.

EWZ had over $8 billion of volume on Monday, the largest notional day in its 25-year history, with a record +$702 million inflow. It has gathered more than $2 billion on the week and AUM is above $11 billion. The underlying index is on track for its best week since 2020. The runoff is Oct 25.

Equal weight has a quiet bid: SPW/SPX is at multi-decade lows and SPY/RSP overlap is at 20-year lows, yet equal-weight positioning remains robust. The SPW vs SPX pair had its best session since summer (+1%) on Thursday.

Fixed income ETFs have been over 20% of all ETF trading volume over the past 10 sessions, nearly double the share from months prior and a record. Munis have collected more than $4.5 billion of inflows in October after a record September. The 10Y yield is 5.24%.

Goldman's Power Up America basket (GSENEPOW) gained 4.9% on the week, with IPPs +12.7% and Power Infrastructure +5.3%. Goldman calls power the most underappreciated AI bottleneck, with positioning at about a 2-year low across themes and IPP and GE Vernova valuations at 2-year lows. Goldman sees behind-the-meter powering 25% of data centers by 2030.

Dated catalysts for the power theme: FERC ruling on the PJM large-load framework on Monday Oct 12, PJM filings and the ERCOT data center interconnection audit. Goldman expects higher earnings revisions as IPPs sign long-term deals with hyperscalers, citing Constellation's about 3.6 GW of nuclear PPAs with Google.

tension_points.bull_case: A market that shrugs off a 5.24% 10Y, a hawkish Fed and an OpenAI revenue scare while hitting new highs wants to go higher. Goldman's Pasquariello makes a version of this case.
tension_points.bear_case: The one trade everyone owns (AI) is also pushing up the cost of capital for everyone else, and a single FT story about OpenAI was enough to rally the long bond. Hedge fund Mag7 exposure is a record 22% with net leverage in the 2nd percentile.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bank earnings and CPI on Tuesday, and TSM a few days later, are the stated tests of whether Thursday's OpenAI scare was also a warning.

tension_points.bull_case: Banks are the most oversold vs the S&P since 1993 (RSI around 27), BKX forward P/E is below its 10-year median, and credit risk is viewed as benign.
tension_points.bear_case: The expected 3Q activity slowdown could be a prolonged slowdown, with CRE as a watch item, and sentiment has turned cautious.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Whether the 3Q activity slowdown proves to be a brief air pocket or a prolonged slowdown in bank earnings.
